To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spin and axial charge of the proton are not equal, that the spin and flavor structure of the proton is well described by a constituent quark model and that the neutron spin structure is well described by the deuteron structure functions.

(a) the neutron spin structure is consistent with that of the proton, (b) the spin of the proton is carried almost exclusively by valence quarks, (c) the axial anomaly is the dominant source of the Bjorkensumrule, and (d) the spin of nucleon in a nucleus is reduced by about 20% relative to that in the free case
the spin of the nucleon is carried by quarks and gluons and that the quark and antiquark distributions in the proton and neutron are not the same.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spin dependent structure of nucleons and the nucleon constituents.
the structure of the nucleons and nuclei, with the aim of understanding the forces between quarks and the origin of hadron masses.
the study of spin dependent structure functions of the nucleon and the deuteron.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the nucleon spin is not a simple sum of the quark and gluon spins.
the spin of a nucleon can be understood in terms of a quark model, but the quark model must include the effects of QCD dynamics.
the spin of the nucleon is not a simple sum of the spins of its quarks, but rather is the result of a subtle interplay between the quark spins and orbital angular momentum.
